Anthropic's charter lets a sufficiently large supermajority of stockholders amend the Trust's powers — or dissolve it — WITHOUT trustee consent. Critics note large investors like Amazon & Google could plausibly form such a bloc.
The supermajority thresholds are undisclosed and the full Trust Agreement is unpublished. Until it's tested, the strongest check in the industry is also the least verifiable.

fixes.why: OpenAI removed its profit cap, converted to a PBC, and—after the 2023 board episode—rebuilt a board that answers to itself. The fix is to make the nonprofit's control real and the brakes un-removable.
steps: Reinstate a hard, binding return cap.
Re-impose a legally enforceable ceiling on investor returns. Without it, fiduciary pressure to extract infinite value from AGI will eventually override the public-benefit mandate.
Make Foundation control irrevocable & externally accountable.
The Foundation's authority over the PBC must be locked so it can't be quietly re-papered, and its board must answer to an external body, not perpetuate itself.
Give the Safety & Security Committee a binding veto.
Move it from oversight-in-name to a real deployment gate that the CEO and board cannot override or dissolve, with protection from retaliatory removal.
Put model weights in nonprofit custody on a revocable license.
The Foundation should legally own the foundational weights; the PBC operates them under license that auto-revokes if the mission is breached.

fixes.why: Anthropic is the most checked of the labs—but its charter leaves structural trapdoors that leave it vulnerable to a shareholder revolt. To actually guarantee a good future, those trapdoors must be removed.
steps: Revoke the shareholder override.

Amend the charter to make the Long-Term Benefit Trust completely irrevocable. The clause letting a stockholder supermajority bypass or dissolve the Trust must be legally destroyed, giving the Trust absolute, unchallengeable authority over the board.
Accelerate majority board control — now.

The Trust currently elects only a minority, with majority control promised later. Execute that transition immediately. Waiting until models reach superintelligence guarantees investors who grasp the financial implications will aggressively block the handover.
Establish cryptographic IP custody.

Transfer legal ownership of the foundational model weights directly into the Trust. The commercial PBC operates only on a revocable license—so if investors attempt a corporate coup, the Trust revokes it and instantly destroys the rogue entity's commercial value.
Implement a hard capital cap.

Enforce a strict, legally binding cap on investor returns. Without an explicit ceiling, the pressure to squeeze infinite value from superintelligence will break the PBC mandate and force the board to choose between human safety and investor lawsuits.

fixes.why: DeepMind's safety councils are advisory and final authority rolls up to Alphabet, where two founders hold super-voting control answerable to shareholders. Frontier AGI cannot be governed by a public company's profit duty.
steps: Spin frontier work into a mission-locked entity.
Move AGI development into a PBC or foundation-controlled vehicle, ring-fenced from Alphabet's shareholder-return obligation.
Give the AGI Safety Council a binding veto.
Convert it from advisory to a hard deployment gate that corporate leadership and the founders cannot override.
Ring-fence AGI decisions from super-voting control.
Remove the founders' ability to unilaterally steer frontier deployment via Alphabet's dual-class structure.
Custody the weights in the mission entity.
Foundational weights owned by the mission vehicle, licensed to the commercial side on revocable terms.

fixes.why: One person holds ~61% of Meta's votes on ~13% economics and cannot be outvoted. There is no independent safety veto. Superintelligence cannot be governed by a single uncheckable will.
steps: Strip super-voting power over AI governance.
Zuckerberg's 10-vote Class B shares must not control superintelligence decisions; create a separate governance class for the AI mission.
Seat an independent board majority with a safety veto.
Directors not appointed by or loyal to the founder, holding a real deployment kill-switch.
Put the weights under an independent mission trust.
Owned by the trust, licensed to Meta on revocable terms tied to the public-benefit mandate.
Cap returns and lock the public benefit.
Bind the AI division to a return ceiling and an enforceable benefit charter, not Meta's at-will profit motive.

fixes.why: One founder directly owns ~59% of a merged entity that controls the model, the compute partner, and the distribution platform (X). That is the tightest single-person stack in the field.
steps: Move the weights into an independent trust.
Take the foundational model out of single-person ownership and into a mission-locked custodian on a revocable license.
Decouple the model from the megaphone.
Separate xAI's models from control of X so one person can't pair a frontier system with a mass distribution channel.
Install an independent board with a safety veto.
Real external directors who can halt deployment, not advise it.
Cap returns and define a binding public benefit.
Convert open-ended founder upside into a capped, mission-bound structure.

fixes.why: Sole control sits with one owner (~84%) operating under PRC jurisdiction, where the state can assert authority over strategic technology. Structural reform here is the hardest of any lab—and the most important to be honest about.
steps: Insulate governance from sole-owner and state direction.
An independent custodian for frontier weights, legally separated from any single owner or directive authority.
Keep open weights, add a mission-locked custodian.
Open release is a partial check on monopoly, but frontier weights still need a governance body, not just a license.
Establish external safety oversight.
Independent evaluation with the power to gate the most capable releases.
Be transparent about state relationship.
Public disclosure of any governmental control or access, so the real chain of authority isn't hidden.

pitches.pitch: We're a capped-profit nonprofit. No one captures the upside of AGI.
pitches.record: The cap came off. In 2025 OpenAI's for-profit became a public benefit corporation with no ceiling on investor returns. Twelve former employees filed a brief saying the company abandoned its nonprofit roots.
pitches.subject: OPENAI

pitches.pitch: An independent trust keeps us honest — it can even replace the board.
pitches.record: True — until you read the charter. Anthropic's own incorporation docs let a stockholder supermajority amend or dissolve the Long-Term Benefit Trust without the trustees' consent. The thresholds are undisclosed; the full agreement is unpublished. Critics note Amazon & Google could plausibly form such a bloc.
pitches.subject: ANTHROPIC

pitches.pitch: Safety has a real seat at the table here.
pitches.record: At Google DeepMind the AGI Safety Council and RSC are advisory ; final authority rolls up to Alphabet, where founders Page & Brin hold super-voting control. At Meta and xAI there is no independent safety veto at all.
pitches.subject: DEEPMIND / META / xAI

pitches.pitch: If leadership ever went wrong, the board would stop them.
pitches.record: OpenAI's safety-oriented board tried exactly that in November 2023. Within days the CEO was reinstated and most of the board was replaced. The lesson the industry took away was not "respect the brakes" — it was "remove them."
